sources.behavior: On load clones script.Parent (the dummy Model) into a local var. Runs an infinite while-true loop (wait(0)) polling script.Parent.Humanoid.Health; if Health<1 it waits 1s, clones the stored original, parents the clone to script.Parent.Parent, calls makeJoints() on it, then removes the original dummy Model. No animation/movement/attack logic; purely a death-respawn watcher tied to the dummy's own Humanoid health.

requirements.reason: Geometry (Parts/Mesh/Head/Torso/Decal) is a stationary, non-humanoid-controlled prop with a fixed CFrame achievable by placement, satisfying most of this requirement. However the embedded Respawn Script watches script.Parent.Humanoid.Health and would clone/respawn the dummy on death, which conflicts with 'no reactive behavior/cannot be defeated'; per the requirement's own acceptance criteria this script must be disabled/excluded, which has not yet been done.

The Model provides distinguishable body parts (e.g. Torso, Head) usable as a hitbox reference, but no source in this component defines or wires a hitbox for server-side overlap/distance checks; that logic is owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task and is not present in this captured asset.

integrationNotes: Disable or remove the 'Respawn' Script (index 18) before placing the dummy so no death/respawn behavior can ever trigger, satisfying the non-reactive stationary requirement; this removal is a proposed integration action, not yet applied.
Torso (index 15) is the most distinguishable body part suitable to designate as the server-side hit-detection hitbox for the pending hitDetectionModule work.
Decal Texture rbxassetid://406436910 on the Torso (index 16) supplies the dummy's canvas heavy-bag visual appearance and is reusable as-is for the requested gym theme.

Humanoid (index 17) remains present on the dummy; ensure no damage-dealing script is ever added elsewhere in the namespace, since even with the Respawn script disabled the dummy should never take or process damage per r_dummy_stationary.
